messages.text:
We can accept the draft’s structure if three operational points are fixed in the schedule.

Subcontractors. The first batch needs an external color specialist under the same confidentiality terms as our staff: written undertaking before access, access limited to that batch, no retention beyond the correction window, and no further disclosure. If a blanket subcontractor right is too broad, limit it to one named color specialist for batch one only, with any later specialist requiring fresh written approval.

Calibration files. Full master images are what the specialist needs for color calibration. If masters are unacceptable, we can work from high-resolution crops that include the color target, a neutral border, and enough of the page edge to judge cast, provided those crops are generated by us and the specialist never receives the full letter image. We need that choice settled before scanning starts.

Access and deletion. Correction access for ten days after each delivery. Working copies deleted at the end of day ten except one backup set. Backups rotate off and are deleted at day 45. No other retention for quality control. Access log available to the archive on request.

Publicity. We will not publish letter content. We do want written consent, in this schedule, for one anonymized process image: no readable text, no donor identifiers, used only to show the scanning workflow. If that consent cannot be given now, publicity stays fully restricted and we drop the image.

Please mark which of the specialist limit, the master-versus-crop choice, the 10/45 deletion schedule, and the single process image you can accept.

- **Specialist access.** We can accept one named color specialist for batch one, subject to the archive’s written approval and a signed confidentiality undertaking before access. Access is limited to the approved calibration material during the correction window, with no further disclosure. Any later batch or specialist requires fresh written approval.
- **Calibration.** For the two restricted collections, use the calibration sheet we supply. The specialist may see a scan of that sheet only. For other collections, we can accept studio-generated, high-resolution crops showing the target, neutral border and enough blank page edge to judge cast. Mask all handwriting and identifying details, flatten the crop and obtain archive approval before release. Full letter masters stay with the studio and archive. Please confirm the separate sheet is sufficient for the restricted collections before scanning them.
- **Access, incidents and deletion.** We accept ten calendar days for corrections after each delivery. By the end of day ten, the studio and specialist must delete all working copies. We propose day 30 after delivery as the deadline for deleting the studio’s single backup set, with access limited to disaster recovery. Keep the access log available on request and provide dated written confirmation at both deletion deadlines, covering the specialist’s copies as well. List a monitored incident contact for each party in the schedule and require the studio to notify the archive within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss or unauthorized access. If day 45 is the earliest your backup system allows, please flag that as an outstanding exception for archive review.
- **Publicity.** Drop the process image. The schedule grants no publicity consent. We would consider an equipment-only photograph with no collection material visible, subject to separate written approval of the exact photograph and its proposed use.

We accept one named color specialist for batch one only, subject to your written approval and a signed confidentiality undertaking before any access. Access is limited to the approved calibration material during the ten-day correction window. No further disclosure. Any later batch or specialist needs fresh written approval.

Calibration. We will not send full letter masters to the specialist. For the two restricted collections, a scan of your calibration sheet alone is sufficient, provided the sheet includes a color target and a neutral reference; we will not scan those collections until you confirm the sheet meets that. For all other collections, we accept studio-generated high-resolution crops showing the target, a neutral border, and enough blank page edge to judge cast, with handwriting and identifying details masked, the crop flattened, and archive approval before release. Masters stay with the studio and the archive.

Access and deletion. Ten calendar days for corrections after each delivery stands. Working copies held by the studio and the specialist are deleted by the end of day ten. Our backup rotation cannot meet day 30: the single backup set is deleted at day 45 after delivery, access limited to disaster recovery. Please treat day 45 as an outstanding exception for archive review. We will keep the access log available on request and give dated written confirmation at both deadlines, covering the specialist’s copies as well. Studio incident contact: the digitization desk, monitored on business days. We will notify the archive within 24 hours of discovering suspected loss or unauthorized access. Please list your monitored incident contact in the schedule.

Publicity. We drop any process image that could show collection material. The schedule grants no consent to publish letter content or collection images. We ask that it expressly allow one equipment-only photograph, with no collection material visible, only after your separate written approval of the exact photograph and its proposed use. If that clause is refused, publicity stays fully restricted.

Please include the agreed batch-one specialist limits and crop approval requirements in the signed schedule. We will supply a calibration sheet with a color target and neutral reference and confirm both in writing before you scan either restricted collection. For those collections, the sheet scan is the only material the specialist may see.

List the archive representative for this pilot as the monitored incident contact. We will provide a direct notification address for the schedule before signature. The 24-hour notice period runs from discovery, including on weekends and holidays.

We accept the ten-calendar-day correction window, deletion of all studio and specialist working copies by the end of day ten after each delivery, access logs on request, and dated written confirmation of deletion at each applicable deadline.

**Day 45 remains the sole outstanding exception.** Please record the request for one disaster-recovery backup set through day 45 as pending archive approval. We need to resolve that exception in writing before signature or scanning.

We accept the equipment-only photograph clause. The studio may submit one photograph with no collection material visible for review. Any use requires the archive’s separate prior written approval of the exact photograph and its proposed use. Signing the schedule grants no publicity consent.

We will put the batch-one specialist limits and the crop rules into the signed schedule. One named color specialist, your written approval and a signed confidentiality undertaking before access, access only to approved calibration material during the ten-day correction window, no further disclosure, and fresh written approval for any later batch or specialist. For the two restricted collections, the specialist sees only a scan of your calibration sheet, and we will not scan those collections until you confirm in writing that the sheet has a color target and a neutral reference. For other collections, only studio-generated high-resolution crops: target, neutral border, and enough blank page edge to judge cast, handwriting and identifiers masked, crop flattened, archive approval before release. Full letter masters stay with the studio and the archive and are not sent to the specialist.

Incident terms are accepted. The archive representative for this pilot is your monitored contact; please insert the direct notification address before signature. Notice is within 24 hours of discovery, including weekends and holidays. Studio contact remains the digitization desk. Access logs on request, and dated written confirmation of deletion at each deadline, including the specialist’s copies.

Correction and working-copy deletion stand: ten calendar days after each delivery, all studio and specialist working copies deleted by the end of day ten.

Day 45 is the only open point, and we need it resolved in the schedule before signature or scanning. Our backup rotation cannot delete earlier. Please approve this written exception: one studio disaster-recovery backup set only, retained through day 45 after each delivery, then deleted; encrypted; no specialist access; restored only for disaster recovery; any restore logged and notified to you within 24 hours; dated written confirmation of deletion at day 45. If that exception is not approved, we cannot start the pilot.

Publicity: the schedule grants no consent to publish letter content or collection images. One equipment-only photograph, with no collection material visible, may be submitted for review; any use requires your separate prior written approval of the exact photograph and its proposed use.

The archive approves the day-45 exception for this pilot. Please include it in the signed schedule. For each delivery, the studio may retain one encrypted backup set solely for disaster recovery and must delete it by the end of day 45 after that delivery. The specialist has no access to the backup. The studio must log each restore, notify the archive within 24 hours of the restore, and provide dated written confirmation of deletion at day 45.

The day-ten deadline still applies to all studio and specialist working copies, with dated written confirmation covering both. This resolves the sole outstanding exception. We will supply the archive’s direct incident notification address for insertion before signature and confirm the calibration sheet in writing before either restricted collection is scanned.

We will insert the approved day-45 exception in the signed schedule in these terms: for each delivery, one encrypted studio backup set, retained solely for disaster recovery and deleted by the end of day 45 after that delivery; no specialist access; each restore logged and notified to the archive within 24 hours; dated written confirmation of deletion at day 45.

The day-ten deadline still applies to all studio and specialist working copies, with dated written confirmation covering both. Batch-one specialist limits, crop and calibration-sheet rules, incident notice, and the equipment-only photograph clause remain as already agreed. The schedule grants no publicity consent.

No terms remain open. We will not scan either restricted collection until you confirm the calibration sheet in writing, and we will not sign until the archive’s direct incident notification address is inserted.
